transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-06 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Olivia Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Natarajan (Atlas - Head ML Infra), Marco Rojas (Atlas SRE), Elena Voss (Atlas Legal)

Autogenerated summary (brief):
Atlas is evaluating Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted for inference across regulated pipelines. Primary asks: guaranteed reserved GPUs, tenant isolation (quarantine), predictable burst handling for accreditation pipelines that spike 4x nightly, and integration constraints for on-prem/private control plane. Legal asked about audit logs and data residency. Next steps: price + modeling, SE deep-dive, customer to share traces.

Topics:
- reserved capacity sizing and prewarm counts
- tenant quarantine / soft isolation for sensitive pipelines
- burst/failover playbooks and fallback to hosted model variants
- encryption/KMS and audit logging for compliance

Action items (auto list):
- Samir to send pricing and burst model spreadsheet
- Olivia to run throughput estimates
- Priya to share traces and details on peak windows

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Samir: Hey thanks everyone for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in, i'm Samir from Redwood, AE. quick agenda — intake on your reserved GPU needs, isolation requirements for the clinical pipelines, and burst behavior. Olivia will walk through a couple of capacity patterns after that.
[00:00:18] Priya: Thanks Samir. We have a bit of background — we run inference for image triage and some NLP extraction. main constraint is the accreditation window at night where we get a 3-4x spike for 20-40 minutes and we need SLA p99 under 600ms for critical routes. also we need clear isolation for PHI pipelines.
[00:00:35] Olivia: Got it. quick clarifying question — do you expect those spikes to be synchronous across models or concentrated on a single heavy model?
[00:00:42] Priya: Mostly concentrated on a heavy image model, call it triage-v2. There are downstream models but the peak is dominated by that single model.
[00:00:50] Marco: Also worth noting we have a nightly backfill that occasionally runs concurrently; if prewarm isn't correct it can preempt production.
[00:01:02] Samir: Right. so two main patterns we usually recommend: reserved pool sized for steady-state throughput + a warm burst pool that can be reserved or burst-to-hosted. We can model counts based on qps and token/sequence lengths — though for images it's batch size and GPU mem that matters more.
[00:01:20] Priya: When you say "burst-to-hosted" — is that automatically fallback to your hosted endpoint, and does that violate data residency / PHI rules?
[00:01:28] Olivia: Good question. we always recommend explicit routing policy in your tenant. By default we can configure routing to never send regulated tenants off-prem. Burst-to-hosted is an option for non-PHI workloads. For PHI you can leverage a warmed reserved burst pool or pre-provision extra capacity in Redwood Dedicated.
[00:01:48] Elena: From legal side, we need to understand audit trails for any fallback — want to see logs that show which tenant was routed and why, timestamps, and KMS key IDs used.
[00:01:57] Samir: Yep, we have audit logs per request level in Dedicated; we'll share the SOC2 module and the private deployment checklist.
[00:02:07] Marco: there's also the question of node-level isolation. If i have multi-tenant nodes, can we 'quarantine' certain pipelines onto fenced nodes so they're essentially single-tenant?
[00:02:15] Olivia: You can. we support tenant fencing options: fully isolated nodes, soft tenancy with cgroups + quota, or logical tenant fencing with encrypted KV spaces. For strict PHI, single-tenant nodes are recommended. the tradeoff is cost.
[00:02:33] Priya: Cost tradeoffs are fine — we're more concerned about operational overhead. How do you do prewarm and eviction? we had issues with preemption in other vendors where our model got OOM'd.
[00:02:44] Olivia: In Redwood Dedicated we have prewarm pools and a hot-reservation that pins model artifacts and a pinned KV cache. eviction is controlled by policy — you can set preemptible vs non-preemptible nodes, and preemption only happens to burst pools if configured. We'll share example policies.
[00:03:02] Marco: Any limits on how big a warm pool can be? we're thinking about a 16-GPU warm pool for the spike window.
[00:03:10] Samir: No hard limits — it's sizing and contract. Question: what's your typical qps per GPU for triage-v2 when batched?
[00:03:19] Priya: It varies — 60-90 requests/s when batched to 8, but p99 varies depending on queueing. our avg seq len isn't applicable since it's images but GPU utilization goes to 95% on spikes.
[00:03:32] Olivia: For imagery, we'd recommend prewarming with model shards and keeping KV cache/mmap mapped. We'll simulate expected throughput once we have your traces.
[00:03:43] Priya: OK, we'll send traces.
[00:03:47] [small cross talk] Elena: just one more legal note - any cross-region fallback? we can't have data leave EU for these pipelines.
[00:03:55] Samir: understood. we can pin region and disable cross-region fallback for those tenants. that's in the routing policy.
[00:04:03] Marco: How do you handle sudden bursts that exceed both reserved and warm pools? do you queue, reject, or spill to hosted (if allowed)?
[00:04:12] Olivia: We support configurable overflow policies: queue-with-timeout, reject-with-backpressure, or overflow-to-hosted/compatible model variant. For regulated tenants we usually set queue-with-timeout and scale up separately through a manual approval flow or pre-provisioned burst.
[00:04:26] Priya: Curious about cold starts — how long does it take to bring up a model on a warm node vs a cold node?
[00:04:33] Olivia: Warm node — seconds to low tens of seconds depending on weights and mmap. Cold node — minutes, unless you have pre-staged artifacts. For LLM-like models there's a memory map step, but our runtime supports continuous batching so warm nodes are near-instant for single-token streams. for images it's mostly model load time and weight mapping.
[00:04:53] [00:05:00] Samir: Reality check — you'll probably need a combination: baseline reserved to cover steady load and the accreditation window plus a small dedicated warm pool sized for the spike; then policy to reject vs overflow. Olivia will run numbers.
[00:05:12] Marco: We're also thinking about network topology: our VPC is peered to a private subnet in GCP; in your Private deployment scenario does the control plane live inside their VPC?
[00:05:23] Olivia: In Redwood Private we can run a customer-controlled control plane that communicates to the inference nodes over private network. For on-prem we ship an appliance or containerized manager you run. For VPC-mode we support private peering and strict egress rules.
[00:05:37] Priya: Any special firewall/NAT requirements? Our security team worries about outbound flows.
[00:05:42] Olivia: Minimal outbound is needed for license checks and telemetry, but it can be restricted to specific endpoints and we have options to whitelist IPs. The private deployment checklist covers ports and egress.
[00:05:54] Elena: About audit logs again: need retention for 7 years and tamper-evident logs for our compliance. Is that supported?
[00:06:02] Samir: We support long-term log export to your S3/GCS with signed artifacts. Tamper evidence can be handled via append-only stores and integration with your SIEM. we'll include docs.
[00:06:12] Marco: Back to isolation — if we have a tenant that we want to 'quarantine' for a week because of a vulnerability, can we migrate that tenant's models to an isolated node quickly? what's the migration cost/downtime?
[00:06:24] Olivia: Migration is usually model rebind: deploy the model artifact into a new node and update routing. With warm pools it can be minutes if artifacts are pre-staged. We can also snapshot KV cache and copy across to reduce cold penalty.
[00:06:38] Priya: So snapshotting the cache — is that safe for PHI?
[00:06:42] Olivia: The cache is encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys if you choose KMS. we can give per-tenant key IDs.
[00:06:50] [00:07:00] Samir: Quick note — a few customers use a hybrid approach: keep the PHI model on single-tenant nodes, and use Redwood Hosted for non-PHI aux models with a compatibility shim. That way burst for non-critical pipelines is cheaper.
[00:07:14] Priya: That seems viable. question — do you have a recommended SLA for warm pools? e.g., 95% avail during spike windows for 30-day rolling?
[00:07:23] Samir: We publish SLA variants for Dedicated, and we can negotiate availability targets tied to reserved capacity. For warm pools we can include prewarm SLOs in contract with a runbook for failover.
[00:07:34] Marco: Also, how do you charge for prewarm nodes when they're idle most of the day? do you have fractional billing?
[00:07:40] Samir: Billing is typically committed monthly for reserved nodes with different tiers for hot vs warm. We can do committed hours or monthly flat fees. We'll include cost modeling in the spreadsheet.
[00:07:51] Priya: On the topic of model variants — if our heavy model can be quantized to run at 2x throughput with ~2% quality loss, can Redwood advise?
[00:07:59] Olivia: Yes, Redwood Optimize can run profile recommendations and quantization suggestions. For image models quantization paths are model-specific; we'll include recommendations after benchmark.
[00:08:10] Marco: Any prebuilt benchmarks for GPUs you run? we saw a benchmark table on your site but it didn't include our specific model family.
[00:08:17] Samir: We'll run a quick micro-benchmark in a trial. Olivia: If you share a small representative checkpoint we can run it behind a signed NDA in our bench cluster and return numbers.
[00:08:30] Priya: Legal question: NDAs, and we can't share PHI. we can anonymize traces.
[00:08:35] Elena: We'll need an NDA first. also ability to have logs only in our account for the trial.
[00:08:41] Samir: Understood. we'll route NDA and we can set trial to export to your S3 for logs.
[00:08:46] [00:09:00] Olivia: i'll summarize the technical checklist we need: traces (qps, batch sizes), model size and checkpoint format, acceptable fallback policies per tenant, region pinning requirements, desired prewarm size.
[00:09:12] Priya: we'll aim to upload traces by end of week.
[00:09:16] Marco: one more ops question: how do upgrades work? if Redwood pushes runtime updates will that cause downtime or model reloads?
[00:09:25] Olivia: Major upgrades are scheduled; we support canary rollout and per-tenant pinning to older runtime for a period. model reloads are non-disruptive in most cases because we can maintain the KV cache and do rolling restarts.
[00:09:39] Priya: good.
[00:09:42] Elena: On data residency again — if we pin region and then you have a catastrophic outage in that region, what's the failover path? we can't just move data without legal approval.
[00:09:50] Samir: For critical regulated tenants, typical pattern is active-passive in same jurisdiction (multi-zone) with DR that uses your approved standby region in same country. We'll document options.
[00:10:04] Priya: Can we get a concrete runbook example?
[00:10:08] Samir: Yes, Olivia will attach a sample runbook with failover steps, required approvals, and estimated RTOs.
[00:10:16] [00:10:30] Olivia: quick tangent — a few customers use quota guards to throttle non-critical pipelines during spikes which keeps the critical p99 in check without extra GPUs. Not ideal but a cost saver.
[00:10:40] Priya: That's an idea. we'll discuss internally.
[00:10:44] Marco: another operational detail — if we pre-stage models across nodes, how do you handle model versions? do we need to pin versions to nodes?
[00:10:52] Olivia: You can pin model versions per-tenant and we support rollouts with canary and A/B. The console shows per-node model mappings.
[00:11:01] Priya: Great.
[00:11:05] Samir: Okay let's move to wrap-up and explicit next steps. I'll send the pricing and burst modeling spreadsheet; Olivia will run throughput estimates once traces are uploaded; Priya will share traces and the legal team will sign the NDA. Any objections?
[00:11:18] Priya: No objections. 
[00:11:20] Elena: We'll read the checklist and NDA.
[00:11:23] Samir: Perfect. final note — we can provision a limited-time reserved trial pool if governance approves. that usually helps demonstrate warm pool behavior.
[00:11:33] Priya: We'll consider.
[00:11:36] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links to SOC2, private deployment checklist, and the spreadsheet.
[00:11:45] Marco: Thanks everyone.
[00:11:47] [call ended]

Meeting recap (auto):
- Atlas needs guaranteed reserved capacity plus warm-prewarm strategies to handle 3-4x nightly spikes for image triage workloads.
- Isolation options: single-tenant nodes recommended for PHI; soft fencing and per-tenant keys available.
- Overflow policies: queue-with-timeout preferred for regulated tenants; overflow-to-hosted only for non-PHI.
- Legal wants audit log retention and tamper-evidence; Redwood to provide docs.
- Next steps and action items documented above.
